Noah (PM): sharing compact timeline mock — we tried compressing rows to fit more versions on small screens. Key questions: canaries still readable? does rollback feel recoverable? https://figma.com/file/abc (screenshots) Priya - Design: Notes on the mock: swapped large percentage block for inline microcopy (e.g., "5% canary") so it doesn't dominate the strip. Added a tiny badge icon to help scanning. Wondering if the inline text is legible at smaller breakpoints. Ethan (frontend): Implementation constraints: when the timeline compresses we lose padding; text may truncate. Options: show full label on focus/hover or collapse to an icon-only mode with accessible label. Performance-wise, prefer avoiding extra network calls for tooltips. Marta (a11y): Accessibility checklist so far: ensure variant label is programmatically associated with percentage (aria-describedby), don't rely on color alone to indicate canary vs stable, and make the rollback control non-destructive language. Suggest announcements for state changes. Example aria pattern: ```
5% canary Variant B, started 10:23am
``` This avoids moving focus unexpectedly while still surfacing info to AT users. Noah (PM): On copy: marketing says "Rollback" triggers fear. Two alternatives proposed: "Undo to last stable" and "Revert traffic to previous". We should A/B test and track cancellation rate + time-to-confirm. Priya - Design: Mocked both CTAs. For the confirmation modal copy I recommend a short summary line + risk line. Example: "Undo to last stable (v19). This will switch live traffic back to v19. No user data will be removed." Then show a small changelog snippet inline. Ethan (frontend): For the modal we're planning a client-side experiment flag: data-experiment="undo-cta" so we can flip wording without a deploy. Also will include keyboard-only focus trap and ESC to cancel. Marta (a11y): Important: ensure the modal uses role="alertdialog" and sets aria-modal="true". On confirm, announce via the live region: "Reverted to version v19. Traffic now at 100 percent." Include clear focus return to the timeline control so keyboard users aren't lost. ci-bot: Canary started: Variant B 5% by noah — build #4821 — ts:1860105475 Priya - Design: tiny UI nit — when several canaries overlap, the inline text becomes crowded. Idea: allow collapsing variant names into numbered tokens and show a legend on hover. This would be hidden by default on mobile. Ethan (frontend): Legend approach ok but keep DOM order predictable for AT. Use visually-hidden legend that becomes visible on expand. Avoid relying on hover-only interactions. Marta (a11y): Also test with screen readers that the timeline ordering makes sense (most recent first vs oldest first). Provide a toggle for chronological order and expose it with a descriptive aria-label. Noah (PM): Action items: Priya to refine 2 compact variants (icon+text vs icon-only with legend), Marta to produce acceptance items and example SR comments, Ethan to prototype listbox + modal behavior with experiment flag, I'll set up an analytics event for "undo_modal_confirmed" and "undo_modal_cancelled". Priya - Design: Uploaded updated mocks (v3) with icon-only compact state and legend behaviour. I'll call out contrast values. Ethan (frontend): I'll hack up a prototype in the sandbox and post a short screencast. Marta (a11y): I'll run quick NVDA/VoiceOver passes on the prototype and share findings. Noah (PM): Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the prototype run-through. If anyone finds edge cases (multi-cluster rollbacks, queued rollouts), drop them here and I'll triage. :white_check_mark:
